title: Tiny to Tall
subtitle: How seeds, bugs, babies and you grow up
subject: Nature

p: Look at a seed in your hand. It is small as a dot.
It looks like nothing. But something is hiding inside.
A whole plant, curled up and waiting.
pages.cap: A seed is a tiny plant in a hard coat.
pages.fact: Did you know? Some seeds can wait for 100 years before they grow.

p: Give the seed water. Give it warm soil.
Crack! A little root pokes out and goes down.
A little shoot pokes out and goes up. Up to the light.
pages.cap: Root down. Shoot up. The seed is awake.

p: You need a dried bean, a wet paper towel and a clear cup.
steps: Fold the wet towel into the cup. Tuck the bean between the towel and the cup.
Put it in a warm spot. Keep the towel wet.
Look every day. In about 5 days you will see a root!
pages.cap: Through the clear cup you can watch the root grow.
pages.safe: Do not eat the bean. Wash your hands after.

p: Leaves open. The plant drinks in light.
Then a bud. Then a flower!
A bee comes to visit. It carries yellow dust from flower to flower. That helps make new seeds.
pages.cap: The bee gets food. The flower gets help making seeds.

pages.q: What does a seed need to start growing?
pages.why: Water and warmth wake the seed up. Then it needs light to keep growing.

pages.h: A giant tree starts as a seed smaller than your fingernail.
p: Look up at the tallest tree you know. It was once a seed you could hold between two fingers.
A tree grows a little every year. Taller. Wider.
Inside, it makes a new ring each year.
Count the rings on a cut tree stump. That is how old it was!
pages.cap: Spring, summer, autumn, winter. One ring for every year.
pages.fact: Did you know? The oldest living tree is more than 4,800 years old.

p: A butterfly lands on a leaf. She leaves a tiny egg.
It is as small as the dot at the end of this line.
Inside, a caterpillar is growing.
pages.cap: The egg is tiny. The caterpillar inside is tinier.

p: Out comes the caterpillar. It is hungry!
It eats leaves all day. It gets fat.
Its skin gets too tight, so it slips out of it. Four or five times!
pages.cap: Eat, grow, change skin. Eat, grow, change skin.

p: The caterpillar hangs upside down.
It makes a hard case around itself. This is a chrysalis.
Inside, something amazing is happening. Shh.
pages.cap: The chrysalis looks still, but inside everything is changing.

p: After about two weeks the case cracks. Wet wings unfold. They dry in the sun. Then, flap, flap, away!

pages.q: What comes right after the caterpillar?
pages.why: Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. The chrysalis comes after the caterpillar.

p: A baby cat is a kitten. A baby dog is a puppy.
A baby cow is a calf. A baby rabbit is a kit.
Which baby animal have you seen?
pages.cap: A baby rabbit is born with no fur and its eyes shut.
pages.fact: Did you know? A newborn kangaroo is the size of a jelly bean.

p: Fish lay eggs in the water. Hundreds of them!
Tiny fish hatch out. They hide in the coral.
They eat, and grow, and grow some more.
pages.cap: Baby fish hide in the reef until they are big.

p: A hen sits on her egg. She keeps it warm.
After 21 days, tap, tap, crack!
Out comes a wet, tired chick. Soon it is fluffy and running about.

v.title: From egg to hen
items: a grown hen lays her own egg

pages.cap: From egg to hen takes about half a year.

p: A baby elephant weighs about 100 kilograms when it is born.
That is as heavy as a big grown-up!
It can stand up on its first day.

v.title: A baby elephant is about as tall as you, but much heavier

pages.cap: A new elephant is about as tall as you are.

p: You need a photo of you as a baby and a mirror.
steps: Look at the baby photo. Look in the mirror.
What is the same? Your eyes? Your smile?
What is different? Your hair? Your teeth? Your size?
pages.cap: You have changed a lot. You are still you.

p: When you were born, you were about 50 centimetres long.
You weighed about as much as a bag of potatoes.
You could not walk or talk. You could cry and sleep!
pages.cap: A newborn baby fits in a grown-up's arms.

p: Now you are about 1 metre tall.
You can run, climb, sing and ask questions.
You grew about 6 centimetres last year. That is about one finger.
pages.cap: You are twice as long as you were as a baby.

pages.why: Everyone starts as a baby. Then they grow and grow.

p: Your bones grow longer. Mostly while you sleep!
Soon a baby tooth will wobble and fall out.
A bigger tooth will grow in its place.
pages.cap: Your bones are growing right now.

p: The biggest dinosaurs hatched from eggs about the size of a grapefruit.
The babies were as small as a cat.
They grew up longer than a bus!
pages.cap: This giant started life as a tiny hatchling.
